paragraph: Englewood's single-family market is the volume driver with 50 sales over six months at a median of $749,500, and the typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial with two full baths. Sales ran from $440,000 up to $7,000,000, so the average of $1,127,430 is being pulled hard by the top end. The median is the number to anchor on. With 54 percent of homes selling above asking, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.006, and a median of 25.5 days on market, this is competitive but not frenzied. Buyers should expect competition on the good ones and room to think on the rest. The monthly series shows medians climbing from $603,750 in February to $768,000 in July on rising volume, which is the normal spring-into-summer build rather than anything unusual. If Englewood follows the usual arc, expect the median to drift as fall closings come in. Condos and townhouses, by contrast, are running softer at 31 sales, a median of $470,000, a 0.989 sale-to-list ratio, and 43 days on market, mostly two-bedroom, two-bath units with a handful of townhouses. Sellers there are pricing to negotiate. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance lifestyle and lower price point of a condo.
